title: Numbers 0–20
objective: Say and understand numbers 0–20 in isolation and in short utterances.
intro_md: [L1: In this lesson you learn the numbers from 0 to 20 — to say them, to hear them, and to read them in short sentences. The '-teen' numbers (13–19) get special attention: they are the ones people mishear most.]
notes: Band map allocates 21 vocabulary items to this lesson: the number words zero-twenty exactly (the noun 'number' itself is budgeted to L11 with phone numbers, so prompts here avoid it and use L1 instructions or digit anchors instead). new_vocabulary.example_sentence: Four letters: N, A, M, E.

exercises.prompt: zero · one · two · three · four · five · six · seven · eight · nine · ten
exercises.rationale: Form-meaning link for 0-10 with audio; split from the teens so each flashcard block stays within working-memory limits.

exercises.prompt: eleven · twelve · thirteen · fourteen · fifteen · sixteen · seventeen · eighteen · nineteen · twenty
exercises.rationale: The teens block, where stress and the '-teen' suffix carry the meaning; sequenced second so the transparent 0-10 forms are already stable.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match the digit to the word.]
exercises.rationale: Base form vs '-teen' form with the digit as anchor: 3/13 and 4/14 are minimal pairs in both script and sound, the exact contrast that corrupts phone numbers later (L11).
Syllable-count discrimination (band pron target P1): final-syllable-dropping L1s (vi, zh) hear 'six' for 'sixteen'; the third option checks vowel quality, not just length.

options.label: six
options.rationale: One syllable — catches listeners who drop the unstressed-looking final syllable.

options.label: fifteen
options.rationale: Same '-teen' ending; forces hearing the first syllable, not just the suffix.

exercises.rationale: Sequence retrieval across the 10-12 boundary where es cognate support ends (once/doce are opaque); 'two/twenty' distractors attack the tw- family confusion head-on.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Put the numbers in order, smallest first.]
exercises.rationale: The four tw-/t- lookalikes in one task: ordering by magnitude forces retrieving each meaning, not pattern-matching the shared onset.

exercises.scoring: case-insensitive; 'seven' scored as mishearing with targeted feedback on the initial unstressed syllable
exercises.rationale: Sound-to-spelling for the eleven/seven rhyme pair: the unstressed initial /ɪ/ is exactly what es ears delete; writing it forces hearing it.

exercises.prompt: [audio] 'Hi! My name is Ana. I'm eleven.' — [L1: Which number do you hear?]
exercises.rationale: Numbers in a short utterance (the objective's second half): the target sits after the known frame 'I'm', training learners to catch numbers inside running speech.

options.label: eleven
options.rationale: Heard after 'I'm' — three syllables, stress on -le-.

options.label: seven
options.rationale: Rhymes with eleven; catches listeners who miss the unstressed first syllable in connected speech.

options.label: ten
options.rationale: Shares the /en/ ending only — checks the learner is not matching final sounds alone.

exercises.rationale: Upper-teens sequence including the exit to twenty; 'eight' catches the base/-teen confusion in production, mirroring ex 4's receptive version.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Count aloud from zero to ten.]
exercises.expected_pattern: zero one two three four five six seven eight nine ten
asr_focus: all eleven numbers present and in order
three not reduced to /triː/ (noted, not failed — /θ/ is a U3 target)
exercises.rationale: Serial production to automatize the 0-10 core; counting is the retrieval structure learners actually use when they need a number in the wild.
